topics.topic: Normative instant at which the backup snapshot is fixed
questions: Which event is the normative instant of a backup: beginning the read transaction or performing the first read that fixes its snapshot?
Is the backup's recorded instant taken when the read transaction is opened, or when its first read fixes the SQLite snapshot?

quotes:
The copy answers, from its one read transaction, the
instant that transaction began and the last sequence number the audit
counter it holds says (A15 rule 5), so a backup's record describes exactly its
copy (A18 rule 1).
judgement.why: One passage assigns the recorded instant to the beginning of the read transaction, while the other assigns it to the later first read that fixes the snapshot.

bases.passage:
The copy answers, from its one read transaction, the
instant that transaction began and the last sequence number the audit
counter it holds says (A15 rule 5), so a backup's record describes exactly its
copy (A18 rule 1).
bases.rests_on:
A backup is a consistent copy of the store taken while Registry runs:
one snapshot of the store, as one read transaction sees it, while other
transactions go on; it never holds part of a transaction, and its
recorded instant and last sequence number are those of that snapshot,
the instant being when its read transaction began.

witness.initial: A backup read transaction has begun but has not yet performed its first read.
events: Registry begins the backup's read transaction at T0.
Another Registry action commits at T1 while the backup reader and writer proceed without waiting for each other.
The backup first reads the audit counter at T2, fixing its snapshot.
outcomes: The backup records T0 because its instant is when the read transaction began.
The backup records T2 because its instant is read when the first read fixes the snapshot.
witness.observer: The owner sees the different instant in the backup record, kept filename and newest-backup display.
basis:
The store runs in
SQLite's write-ahead-log mode, in which a reader and the writer never
wait for each other, so no write waits for, or is refused or fails for,
a copy, nor a copy for a write.

topics.topic: Ownership and same-connection reading of the backup snapshot audit counter
questions: Which module owns reading the audit counter that fixes the backup snapshot, and how is that read made on the same backup read connection without reversing the declared dependency or giving the fact two owners?

quotes:
`capability:store.copy_store_snapshot` writes one
   read snapshot of the store, the agent sessions removed, at the temporary
   path `module:backups` named, and answers the last sequence number the
   audit counter holds — the read that fixes the snapshot — with the instant
   read from the clock at it (A18 rules 1, 2, A15 rule 5);
judgement.why: State 4 assigns the snapshot-consistent audit-counter read to `store.copy_store_snapshot`, which performs it as the read that fixes the same snapshot and returns the value to `backups`.
